Luca Guadagnino has to return some videotapes. The Oscar-nominated director is passing on Scott Z. Burns ' American Psycho adaptation.

While appearing on Deadline's Crew Call podcast, Guadagnino told Anthony D'Allesandro that he is no longer attached to the projects, two years after we exclusively revealed he and Burns were adapting Bret Easton Ellis' 1991 novel .

"Scott Z. Burns wrote a fantastic script," said Guadagnino. "Unfortunately for me, as we speak, it's not happening."

In October 2024, Deadline revealed that Guadagnino was in final talks with Lionsgate to direct Burns' adaptation, which would be produced by Frenesy Films, and executive produced by Sam Pressman, the son of Edward R. articles.title: No Matter What Happens Next With Batman, This Reeves-verse Cliffhanger Needs to Be Resolved
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Warner Bros. Robert Pattinson’s casting as the next James Bond has made his future as Batman even more uncertain. There was already a considerable amount of doubt about whether the British star would play the role of Bruce Wayne for a third time, despite his frequently mentioned enthusiasm for the character, after the numerous lengthy delays to […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Robert Pattinson’s casting as the next James Bond has made his future as Batman even more uncertain. There was already a considerable amount of doubt about whether the British star would play the role of Bruce Wayne for a third time, despite his frequently mentioned enthusiasm for the character, after the numerous lengthy delays to Matt Reeves’ The Batman: Part II , and many have seen Pattinson taking on the lead role of the Bond franchise as an especially clear indication that his time as DC’s most popular superhero is coming to an end. But even if this is true, there’s at least one more story other than Part II that needs to be told to give fans of Reeves’ version of Gotham City closure.

Two years after The Batman ’s release, its TV spin-off The Penguin became a massive hit for HBO. Taking place shortly after the film, the series depicted a conflict between Colin Farrell’s version of the titular supervillain, also known as Oswald “Oz” Cobb and Sofia Falcone (Cristin Milioti.) The series received widespread critical acclaim and Sofia quickly emerged as its breakout character, with both Farrell and Milioti winning Emmys for their performances. Sofia’s storyline ends with a tantalizing cliffhanger setting up a future encounter between her and her half-sister, The Batman ’s Selina Kyle/Catwoman (Zoë Kravitz,) and regardless of what else is in store for Bruce and Gotham’s onscreen futures, DC still needs to follow up on this promise, whether with another series or film.

As Batman, Bruce first encounters Selina while interrogating Oz at his criminal nightclub, The Iceberg Lounge, where she works. After following her and learning of her skills as a cat burglar, Bruce recruits Selina to help him investigate the string of high profile murders committed by the Riddler (Paul Dano,) which are connected to both the city’s organized crime and the disappearance of Selina’s friend and roommate Annika Kosolov (Hana Hrzic.) It is eventually revealed that Selina’s biological father is Oz’s employer, mob boss Carmine Falcone (John Turturro,) who murdered both Selina’s mother and Annika. Having led Bruce to expose Falcone’s control over the city’s government, Riddler kills Falcone as part of a planned revolt against Gotham’s largely corrupt wealthy class. After helping Bruce stop the insurrection, Selina leaves Gotham.

The Penguin reveals that Falcone (a younger version of whom is played by Mark Strong) had murdered several other women, including his wife, Sofia’s mother, in similar ways. Ten years before the events of the film and series, reporter Summer Gleason (Nadine Malouf) approached Sofia with evidence of her father’s crimes. When Sofia began helping Summer investigate, Oz, who was working as her driver at the time, informed Carmine, who then had Sofia herself framed for the murders and committed to Arkham Asylum, where she endured further, horrific abuse. After her release, Sofia assassinates all the relatives who were aware of her innocence and takes control of the remains of Carmine’s criminal empire, renaming it and herself with her mother’s maiden name of Gigante. But after the pair begin feuding in a gang war, Oz successfully frames her for other crimes with the help of corrupt law enforcement officials, and Sofia is sent back to Arkham. In her final scene in the series, Julian Rush (Theo Rossi,) a psychiatrist with a romantic fixation on Sofia delivers her a letter from Selina, which makes Sofia smirk despite her bleak circumstances.

The Penguin was initially conceived as a limited series and despite frequent rumors to the contrary , a second season has never been officially announced for development. Farrell is set to return as Oz in The Batman: Part II , but Reeves and Milioti herself have confirmed that she will not appear as Sofia in the film. Kravitz is also not among the cast members confirmed to be returning alongside Pattinson, with Scarlett Johansson having instead been cast as a new character widely believed to be the sequel’s female lead. If Selina does turn out to have a secret role in the film, it’s likely to be much smaller than the one she had in the first. Narratively this makes sense, as Part II is also said to take place shortly after the first film and Selina’s departure. But given the Bond casting and unexpected recent changes at DC Studios, concern is growing that Part II could be the last installment in the so-called “Reeves-verse,” before a possible reboot of the cinematic Batman mythology, which would frustrate viewers by leaving them without answers as to how Selina and Sofia’s stories progress.

DC Studios reportedly turned down pitches for series focusing on Catwoman and Poison Ivy recently. However, it’s not clear if the former featured Kravitz’s version of Selina, specifically, and it was subsequently announced that The Penguin creator Lauren LeFranc is now in the early stages of developing a Poison Ivy series . Given this, the even greater popularity of the Catwoman character, and the acclaim and accolades already received by The Batman , The Penguin , and Milioti specifically, one imagines that executives may be willing to reconsider making a Catwoman project if it features both Falcone sisters. The casting of Johansson and multiple other new actors suggest that Part II may focus less on the Falcone family and other established antagonists, aside from further confrontations between Bruce and Oz. But even if that is true, the Falcones’ influence on Gotham will still be responsible for setting the larger saga in motion, so a project in which Selina and Sofia continue to grapple with Carmine’s legacy could be a fitting conclusion for the franchise.

Sofia’s story is one that seems like it will inevitably end in some kind of tragedy, but leaving the character in Arkham again, indefinitely, is arguably too bleak a conclusion to be satisfying, even for such a dark franchise. A Catwoman project could mostly follow her and Selina outside of Gotham, once Sofia is out of the asylum, but if such a project were to be the last in the Reeves-verse it would ideally also involve Bruce and some of the other major established characters, though the story should of course remain rooted in the sisters’ perspectives. Bruce acting as a supporting character would make involving Pattinson despite the Bond casting easier, and a smaller role like those he plays in the movies could likewise entice Farrell to return despite his mixed feelings on the extensive makeup and prosthetic effects used to portray Oz, assuming that character survives Part II .

Do you think DC should give The Batman a Catwoman spin-off? Discuss in the comments.

articles.title: 20 Years Ago, Bleach's Dub Forever Changed a Major Plot Twist & Fans Didn't Even Notice
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Studio Pierrot Bleach Episode 62 features some of the most crucial moments in the entire series. The episode was originally released in Japan on December 20th, 2005, before getting its English release on September 8th, 2006. However, the English dub carried a subtle yet crucial change from the original version that forever ruined a major plot twist […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Bleach Episode 62 features some of the most crucial moments in the entire series. The episode was originally released in Japan on December 20th, 2005, before getting its English release on September 8th, 2006. However, the English dub carried a subtle yet crucial change from the original version that forever ruined a major plot twist of the story. The debate centering around anime subs and dubs has been going on for decades, and there’s really no way to determine which is overall better. Many English-speaking fans find it easier to follow through with a story in a language they are familiar with rather than reading subtitles constantly.

Anime from the 1990s and 2000s especially relied on English dub during TV broadcasts to attract more viewers in the West. Unfortunately, there have been many such cases where the dubs fail to capture the true essence of the story. This is also the case for Bleach, where the dub of Episode 62 changed a crucial moment between Gin and Rangiku. They're two of the most beloved characters in the series, especially Gin, who became even more popular after the truth behind his actions came to light in the Fake Karakura Town. However, fans watching the dub missed a crucial hint that Episode 62 dropped before he bid farewell to Rangiku.

The Soul Society Arc is often considered to be one of the best parts of the story, especially since this is when the series gets more intense. Bleach expands its world-building and introduces Sosuke Aizen as one of the most dangerous villains in the story. Along with Aizen, two Squad Captains also betrayed the Soul Society, including Gin Ichimaru. Initially portrayed as a villain, it wasn't until the Fake Karakura Town that the series revealed Gin only wanted to defeat Aizen by any means necessary. He also wanted to get back the fragment of the Soul King Aizen stole from Rangiku.

During Episode 62, Rangiku tries to stop Gin from leaving Soul Society, but the Menos Grande from Hueco Mundo emits a light called Negacion that would seriously injure other Soul Reapers if they touch it. Gin quickly pushed her away so she wouldn't get hurt, but also didn't forget to taunt her that he didn't mind being her prisoner for a little while longer. However, things actually became more interesting when he said, “Maybe next time.” This is completely different from the subbed version where he actually apologizes to her.

Gin also couldn't hide the sorrow on his face, so saying, “I'm sorry,” actually made a lot more sense in that moment. The subbed version also puts into perspective that betraying Rangiku deeply hurt him, but there wasn't another path he could've chosen. Not only that, but this scene also makes fans realize that Gin wasn't always portrayed as a heartless snake. The hints were always there, which is all the more reason the plot twist was so heartbreaking yet exceptionally well-written.

Did you notice the difference between the Bleach sub and dub in Gin's farewell to Rangiku? Do you think the change affected the emotional impact of the scene? Share your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: Battlestar Galactica Is the Best TV Series of the 2000s and Nothing Has Even Come Close to It Since
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Syfy TV in the 21st century reached new levels of quality. Television in the 20th century was looked at as lesser than both film and the stage, and for a long time it was the home of fluff. However, as the years went by, more and more TV shows got better, more complex, more engrossing than […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google TV in the 21st century reached new levels of quality. Television in the 20th century was looked at as lesser than both film and the stage, and for a long time it was the home of fluff. However, as the years went by, more and more TV shows got better, more complex, more engrossing than ever before. The '90s had shows like X-Files, Oz, Star Trek: Deep Space Nine , while future classics like The Sopranos, Sex in the City , and Six Feet Under began. These shows formed the basis of what has been called the Golden Age of Television, which began in the '00s. There are some brilliant shows from the first decade of the 2000s, but there's one show deserves the title of best TV show of the '00s: Battlestar Galactica .

The original Battlestar Galactica was network TV's answer to Star Wars , a show that definitely looked and felt like it was from the late '70s in the worst ways. While it had its fans, it just never found a big enough audience for how much it cost to make and would become one of many lost sci-fi series. However, Ronald D. Moore, one of Star Trek 's best writers, and David Eick would end up bringing the show back on the then-Sci-Fi Channel in 2004, starting with a four-part miniseries. Battlestar Galactica isn't a perfect show – some fans find its last season disappointing – but it really is the best show of the decade, beating out numerous amazing shows for the title.

The early '00s were a great time to be watching TV. HBO Sundays were becoming the home of the best TV shows around, the networks were putting out shows like 24 and Lost , and Adult Swim on Cartoon Network was making adult animation into a force to be reckoned with. The Sopranos was the 500-pound gorilla in the room, but it felt like there was something amazing on TV every night. The '90s had been the decade of cable, with many new channels popping up, as well, broadening the mixture of shows.

The Sci-Fi Channel launched in 1992, playing reruns of old sci-fi and genre shows. Eventually, they started to make their own original series and Moore and Eick pitched the network the reboot. Sci-Fi wanted the show and casting would begin in Canada. The show was meant to be the focus of a new programming slate, using a recognizable old name to get fans old and new through the door.

The original Battlestar Galactica saw the titular ship escape the destruction of the Colonies at the hands of Cylons, leading a fleet of civilians ships into the stars to find the original home of humanity – Earth. The new series would copy this idea, using many of the same names of characters, ships, and places, but changed everything else. The original Battlestar Galactica was a Star Trek/Star Wars style sci-fi universe, but the BSG reboot would take place in a more grounded universe. Gone were the weird alien races, the lasers, and the bizarre clothes. In their place were the Greek Gods, a whole lot of ammunition, and fashion that looked like it stepped out of 2004 Vancouver (because it did).

Moore and Eick wanted to use the series to talk about the then-current War on Terror. The Cylons were the creations of humanity who had rebelled. The first war almost destroyed humanity, but the Cylons retreated out of nowhere leading to decades of detente. The miniseries takes a page from the 9/11 playbook, as the Cylons launch a massive sneak attack on the Colonies of Man, slaughtering billions, with only the Galactica and a fleet of civilian ships escaping. The ship rearmed and then set course past the Red Line – the edge of known space – as they searched for the homeworld of mankind, Earth.

The show starred Edward James Olmos, Katee Sackhoff, Mary McDonnell, Jamie Bamber, Michael Hogan, James Callis (Baltar is the best), Tricia Helfer, and numerous others. The original series was the brainchild of Glenn Larson and it was very Mormon. Moore and Eick went in a completely direction, with the Colonials being polytheistic worshipers of the Lords of Kobol, our Greek Gods, while the machine Cylons were monotheistic, worshiping the one "true" god. This focus on religion and culture was different from any other sci-fi show out there, giving it a unique flavor.

The show was military sci-fi with a religious edge. Back in the early '00s, the right was selling the War on Terror as a clash of civilizations and Moore and Eick took the show in that direction, while also showing how foolish that was by the end of the story. The characters were able to inhabit their roles perfectly, and as the episodes dug into them, their past, and the trauma of the destruction of mankind, we watched them change and grow. It felt like nearly every character had an arc of some kind; they all started in one place and ended up in a complete other (in more ways than one).

Of course, there are some complaints that the show can't duck. To begin with, Moore and Eick had no plan on how to end the series and when you rewatch it, it shows. The last season is an interesting beast because it does tie up all the plot threads, but the way it did it made a lot of fans angry. Without getting too into the weeds of it all, the show went to places that sci-fi fans, one of the atheist/agnostic fandoms out there, didn't really like. The final episode is one you either love completely or don't like at all (I personally love it and have watched it more than any other finale, but I get why other people don't like it). However, I think the flaws of the show make it what it is. It's one of the best rides in TV history, and was able to be more interesting than anything else in the decade.

The '00s had three of the best TV shows of all-time – The Sopranos, Mad Men, and Breaking Bad . The shows all had the same throughline – a badly behaving patriarch – and gave viewers some of the best performances imaginable. You can point to all of them as nearly flawless examples of everything that TV should be. However, I think that even though it definitely had its flaws, Battlestar Galactica was better than all of three of them.

To begin with, it became appointment TV in a way those shows didn't. Friends would get together to watch it every week. The fandom was so engaged by the show, helped along by Moore and Eick using the Internet to communicate more with them. It honestly felt like a true fan community

The show had a lot to say about the moment in time that was the '00s, letting us take a step back from the goings on of the day and see it from another perspective. It had characters that you fell in love with; sure, those other shows all had great characters, but could you love them? Most of them were monsters of some kind. The characters of BSG were flawed, stressed out, traumatized, and exhausted, but they were good people in a terrible situation. TV reboots can be all over the place , but Battlestar Galactica was able to create an amazing narrative peopled by brilliant characters in a way that no other show of the decade could.

What do you think of Battlestar Galactica ? Who's your favorite character and why is it Baltar? Who did you ship with Kara (the only right answer is Anders)? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: After 31 Years, This Legendary Sci-Fi Anime Movie Still Has No Worthy Competition
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Production I.G. During a career spanning over forty years, Mamoru Oshii became a pioneering anime director and filmmaker, best known for his incredible work in the Ghost in the Shell franchise. While the legendary director has been a part of the industry since the 1980s, he got his global breakthrough thanks to the Ghost in the Shell film in 1995. The […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google During a career spanning over forty years, Mamoru Oshii became a pioneering anime director and filmmaker, best known for his incredible work in the Ghost in the Shell franchise. While the legendary director has been a part of the industry since the 1980s, he got his global breakthrough thanks to the Ghost in the Shell film in 1995. The film not only became a massive hit in Japan, but it made Oshii globally renowned after catching the attention of fans in the United States and Europe. Oshii is particularly famous for his distinctive , philosophy-oriented storytelling, along with artistic style, sometimes even prioritizing visuals over the plot.

Before his greatest sci-fi movie, he made his directorial debut in 1983 with the Urusei Yatsura: Only You film, and then released another film of the franchise in the following year. Ghost in the Shell premiered in Japan on November 18th, 1995, exactly 31 years ago. It's safe to say that the film has had no worthy competition over the decades. This also applies to the anime remake by Science SARU , which was one of the biggest hits of the year. While the remake was a more faithful adaptation of the acclaimed manga by Masamune Shirow, Oshii took liberties in his storytelling, making it stand out from other anime.

Due to the advancement in technology, modern animation has changed significantly over the years. Unlike the animation from a few decades ago, animators rely mostly on a blend of traditional hand-drawn animation with digital techniques, primarily using CGI for lighting, coloring, backgrounds, and motion. This allows the animators to include more details in each frame, creating a unique sense of depth and aesthetic appeal. However, while modern animation has its perks, it’s evident that modern technology can’t create such intricate details as seen in the older anime , especially something as artistic as Ghost in the Shell .

The film is a pioneer of new animation techniques, known for its stunning visuals through the use of a blend of traditional cel animation with early computer-generated imagery. The anime industry largely moved from traditional cel animation to digital pipelines in the early 2000s, completely changing the art style and the grainy visuals that fans appreciate from the 1990s anime even now. Not to mention that Ghost in the Shell is one of those rare cases where changes from the manga can be seen as a more intriguing method of storytelling, especially if you realize what kind of vibe Oshii was going for.

Oshii's adaptation took a much darker tone than the original manga, especially with the protagonist Motoko Kusanagi. Although she is more cheerful in the manga, her personality in the movie suited the intense themes in the movie, especially considering its futuristic setting. It wasn't just her, but the overall manga had a much more cheerful and warm vibe all the while portraying the problems within the futuristic society.

Do you think any modern sci-fi anime has come close to matching Ghost in the Shell ? What makes this legendary sci-fi movie so timeless? Share your thoughts in the comments!

articles.title: 4 Forgotten Sci-Fi Movies That Were Too Strange for Hollywood (& 1 Was Almost Impossible to Market)
articles.summary: Sci-fi is a genre that allows you to experiment with all kinds of ideas, but not every movie manages to be creative enough to make people want to watch it. Sometimes, the story is so ambitious that you can't follow all the way through, or it features sequences so wild that they barely make any […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Sci-fi is a genre that allows you to experiment with all kinds of ideas , but not every movie manages to be creative enough to make people want to watch it. Sometimes, the story is so ambitious that you can't follow all the way through, or it features sequences so wild that they barely make any sense. There's nothing wrong with trying something different, but going too far outside the box can make it harder to connect with mainstream viewers.

Throughout the decades, Hollywood has released quite a few examples of this , but some were so unusual and weird that they never really gained much popularity or recognition . They have their merits, but they're definitely not for everyone.

The craziest thing about Repo Man is that, despite having good reviews from both critics and audiences, it was totally forgotten to the point where some people don't even know it exists. It eventually became a cult classic (and a pretty niche one at that), following Otto (Emilio Estevez), a young punk with no real plans for the future who ends up working as a car repossessor alongside Bud (Harry Dean Stanton). It's an ordinary job until the two start hunting for a 1964 Chevrolet Malibu with radioactive cargo hidden in its trunk. That's when government agents, rival repo men, and even extraterrestrials show up. But even though what all of this might suggest, the movie isn't exactly a Back to the Future -style sci-fi adventure .

In reality, Repo Man has a very unusual sense of humor, mixing social commentary on consumerism, political satire, and punk culture without worrying too much about making everything fit together. So the obvious questions come in: it's a movie with aliens, but it's not really an alien invasion story? It's a comedy, but not the kind audiences are used to? Finding the right way to market the film proved difficult, and at some point it was even presented as a romantic comedy, which didn't help much. It only started gaining recognition among certain audiences over time, thanks to word of mouth and its soundtrack. It's a distinctive film with personality, but the extremely offbeat approach makes it a tough sell.

If you had to explain The Adventures of Buckaroo Banzai Across the 8th Dimension to someone in just a few sentences, it would be impossible, which was exactly the problem Hollywood faced when trying to sell this movie. It revolves around Buckaroo Banzai (Peter Weller), a neurosurgeon, physicist, test pilot, and rock musician who also leads a group of scientists known as the Hong Kong Cavaliers—yes, he really does all of that. And when Buckaroo tests a vehicle capable of crossing dimensions, he discovers an alien threat: the Red Lectroids, who are planning to invade Earth and are led by John Whorfin (John Lithgow), an extraterrestrial trapped inside a human scientist's body. Like Repo Man , this movie is a mix of a little bit of everything.

So go into this experience expecting conspiracies, interdimensional travel, rock bands, some rather eccentric characters, and a whole bunch of ideas that don't always come with an explanation. It seems to think you already know this universe, even if you're watching everything for the first time. Basically, the whole story is a mess, and that made it super difficult to figure out how to sell it to audiences. In the end, Buckaroo Banzai was marketed as a sci-fi adventure but disappointed at the box office. On the other hand, all that narrative chaos is what won some people over years later , and the experience might actually get better on a rewatch. It's a peculiar feature.

Liquid Sky is an indie production, and a pretty exotic one considering its subject matter. When we think about aliens, we're used to seeing spaceships, invasions, and complex discussions, but this movie has something else in mind. It follows Margaret (Anne Carlisle), a model involved in New York's underground scene in the '80s . Her life is already chaotic, but things get crazier when a small alien spacecraft lands on the roof of her apartment building. These visitors then start targeting people who experience moments of pleasure, causing their victims to disappear. And if that premise sounds bizarre, the rest of the movie is just as strange, although it uses all that strangeness to explore some relevant issues from the time.

The story touches on topics like punk culture, sexuality, drugs, and gender identity, all wrapped in a very specific aesthetic of extravagant outfits, heavy makeup, and neon colors. You could say that Liquid Sky was ahead of its time in many ways, which is also part of why it was considered so weird. Because of that, not everyone back then wanted to watch a sci-fi film that was more focused on exploring New York's nightlife than the aliens themselves. Naturally, it struggled to attract an audience, and its marketing strategy eventually had to shift toward adults and viewers interested in alternative productions. In the end, that paid off.

Did you know Sean Connery starred in a movie that went very wrong? After spending much of his career playing James Bond , he showed up in Zardoz wearing a red loincloth, leather boots, and suspenders. That's strange enough, right? But there's more. The story takes place in 2293, in a post-apocalyptic world divided between the Exterminators, warriors who worship an entity called Zardoz, and the Eternals, an isolated society that has managed to achieve immortality. Zed (Connery) is one of these warriors who eventually goes to the Eternals' territory and finds out their perfect way of life actually comes with a whole set of problems. Through this premise, the movie sets out to explore moral questions, religion, social control, sexuality, and the future of humanity.

However, Zardoz has so many things to say that it gets lost in its own ideas. There are philosophical debates, religious symbolism, some bizarre situations, and visual choices that are hard to make sense of. And while having Connery as the lead could have been a great selling point, his unexpected appearance only made the movie even more confusing for some people. Ultimately, the production performed terribly and received mostly negative reviews (a reputation that has followed it over the years). Some of its ideas are actually quite interesting, but they needed to be developed in a way that could keep the audience engaged. You can certainly find people who enjoy it, but it's one of those features that falls into the "it's so crazy, it's good" category .

That certainly rings true for the actors who were instrumental in kicking off a new era of comic book movies. It's even more meaningful for the die-hard Marvel fans who are excited about the return of the original X-Men to the big screen in Avengers: Doomsday . Professor X, Magneto, Cyclops, Mystique, and Nightcrawler are part of a reunion that, at one point, seemed to be a crossover Hollywood would never see.

And yet, getting everyone to slip right back into their old roles wasn't necessarily an entirely enjoyable experience on set. The returning actors have described rather different experiences, in some cases, when it comes to being a part of this new Marvel blockbuster. One of the returning mutants has shed some interesting light on why this much-anticipated comeback felt, in many ways, like a far cry from the full-cast reunion fans had been hoping for. Regardless, it wasn't a terrible experience by any means, but it's definitely worth taking a deeper dive into some accounts of what supposedly happened behind the scenes.

The most noteworthy piece of information surrounds actor Alan Cumming's involvement, as he makes his return as Nightcrawler after he was introduced as the teleporting mutant in 2003's X2 . Cumming said that the returnees didn't spend quite as much time together as fans may have thought. Much of the filming was done on separate sets and in different locations, meaning the returning actors didn't necessarily get to spend time chatting as old friends between takes, as many fans may have originally imagined. Still, the rapport hasn't deteriorated, as Cumming has maintained relationships with many of his co-stars over the years. And who can forget the trailer when Nightcrawler was first revealed? I remember I was super hyped when I first saw it.

There's even a fascinating history behind these friendships. Cumming has already spoken about the trouble he had in makeup when filming X2 , in order to be turned into Nightcrawler . Though the production left its mark on the cast, it also created bonds that lasted long after filming wrapped. Cumming has described his reentry into the Marvel franchise as far more jovial, especially compared to all the reasons he had for leaving the character in the first place. Clearly, it's been a whole lot more fun to get back into makeup and costume when things around the actor are starting to look up.

This reunion is also particularly meaningful to those who have been in the superhero fandom for a long time. X-Men 's 2000 adaptation came nearly a decade before the start of the Marvel Cinematic Universe with 2008's Iron Man . Patrick Stewart and Ian McKellen set the stage for two of the most iconic characters in the genre with Professor X and Magneto. James Marsden gave an unforgettable performance as Cyclops, Rebecca Romijn was Mystique, and Cumming went on to play Nightcrawler in the follow-up, X2 . Overall, those actors created the foundation for the superhero movies that would come after. Kevin Feige himself was an associate producer on the original X-Men .

It also makes it easier to come to terms with the working conditions of these reunion productions, with Marsden also having spoken of his joy at being able to see his previous co-stars again and Romijn having noted that her return to Mystique was a very surreal one. Still, it does partly take some of the sting out of the production's frankly inconsistent reunion plans. Even if they weren't all in the same place every day, they still got to do this for at least some time, and that part of it really is pretty special, especially given the chance to see Patrick Stewart return as Professor X one final time in what will now be his final on-screen appearance. Avengers: Doomsday will premiere on December 18, 2026, bringing together the different generations of Marvel characters for everyone who grew up on the first mutants. For those who remember the old days, it isn't just a hero showdown; it is a chance to think about the dawning of a new chapter.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The MCU is no stranger to breaking records, as many of the franchise's movies have gone on to become overwhelming box office hits. However, Spider-Man: Brand New Day is on track to break one of the most impressive records in movie history, and it'll never be done again.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day has been a huge box office success , with it not only becoming the highest-grossing solo superhero movie of all time, but also the third highest-grossing movie ever. The film has made $2.52 billion so far, and if things go according to Marvel's plans, that'll be far from its final total.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day is getting a rerelease , and it will hit theaters on Friday, December 4. The rerelease is set to include 10 minutes of new footage that wasn't seen in the film's original theatrical run, including a cut scene that features the return of Rosario Dawson's Claire Temple from Daredevil . This is incredibly exciting for fans, as the return of this cameo and several other cut moments could make the already great film even better.

However, Brand New Day 's rerelease is also incredibly exciting for Marvel Studios. During the film's original theatrical release, Spider-Man: Brand New Day grossed $959 million domestically, making it the highest-grossing film at the domestic box office of all time. The fourth MCU Spider-Man film passed other big hits, like the previous record holder, 2015's Star Wars: Episode VII - The Force Awakens , as well as 2019's Avengers: Endgame , and even 2021's Spider-Man: No Way Home .

What could make things even more impressive is that, if the rerelease makes only $41 million, Spider-Man: Brand New Day will become the first film to cross $1 billion at the domestic box office. While plenty of films have hit this number worldwide, it has yet to be done domestically, at least as of the writing of this article. While future movies could also pass this milestone domestically, Brand New Day has the chance to be the only film that can claim that it did it first.

It isn't a stretch for Brand New Day to make more than $41 million, based on Marvel's previous rereleases. Avengers: Endgame Encore , the 2026 rerelease of the 2019 conclusion to the Infinity Saga, made $40.1 million domestically. So, Brand New Day just has to barely surpass this in order to meet this goal. The rerelease will hit theaters mere weeks before Doomsday 's release, and the hype of the crossover could help boost Brand New Day 's box office. It will be close, but this could make Brand New Day 's rerelease an even more significant box office moment than Doomsday 's.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day will be the third MCU film to get an enhanced rerelease, after 2022's Spider-Man: Brand New Day - The More Fun Stuff Version and 2026's Avengers: Endgame Encore . Each of these rereleases has given their original films a second wind, helping to pad the box office and extend their cultural relevance. This experiment seems to be paying off for Marvel, as the number of rereleases has gone from a coincidence to a pattern.

So, if Brand New Day 's rerelease is more successful than Endgame Encore , it wouldn't be surprising to see more rereleases drop in the future. For example, 2025's The Fantastic Four: First Steps would be the perfect candidate for a rerelease. We know that lots of footage was left out of The Fantastic Four , including John Malkovich's Red Ghost. The film wasn't as big of a box office hit as Marvel had hoped, but now that Doomsday is boosting the popularity of these characters, the MCU could capitalize on this by releasing the film again. Adding in these cut scenes would warrant a viewing from preexisting fans, while one last shot at a theatrical experience could simultaneously bring new fans in.

It is also possible that Marvel could have designed Avengers: Doomsday with an Encore cut in mind. 2027 could see the film get a rerelease ahead of Secret Wars , this time with more cameos or a cut fight scene. While pre-planning an enhanced edition may seem a bit more scummy than making one out of footage that just so happened to be dropped from the original cuts, it is impossible to rule out this possibility.

Which Marvel films do you want to see an Encore cut of? Let us know on the ComicBook Forum !

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There's no denying that Solo Leveling  is the most popular and influential webtoon and light novel series of all time. It also paved the path for the entire medium’s success across the globe, encouraging more animation studios to release webtoon adaptations. This is all thanks to the success of the anime adaptation by A-1 Pictures, as it became one of the biggest hits in history.  Solo Leveling  isn’t the first manhwa to get an anime adaptation, but no South Korean series pushed the medium to this level of global popularity as it did. Following the second season’s conclusion last year,  the anime announced its sequel movie  during this year’s Anime Expo.

However, while fans await the anime's return, its biggest competitor is also planning a huge comeback. Along with Solo Leveling,  Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint  is often considered just as globally renowned. The series has already confirmed an anime adaptation in 2024, and it’s already one of the most anticipated series right now. While the anime is currently under production, the webtoon is ongoing, and it's all set to return with its anticipated second season.

Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint will be released on November 24th, 2026. The official X handle of REDICE Studio only shared the Korean release date, along with a 30-second teaser. The first season of the webtoon went on a hiatus in May this year with the release of Chapter 311. The season ends on a huge cliffhanger, as it marks a major turning point in the series while stopping near the end of the Demon King Selection arc. The second season will kick off from where the story left off and wrap up the ongoing arc before moving on to the next one.

The webtoon has already adapted almost half of the web novel, so if the second season releases around the same number of chapters, then this will be the final season of the series. While the series is returning with a new season for Korean fans, the English platform Webtoon is also continuing to release the translations after several months. The serees went on a hiatus after the English release of Chapter 308 in June this year, but the next chapter was finally released on November 21st, 2026. We can expect the remaining two chapters to drop on the platform before the English debut of Season 2.

Although it's been more than two years since the anime adaptation was announced, fans still have no idea when it will be released. Previously, the anime was expected to debut in 2027, but a report by  Com2uS’ website confirmed the wait will be longer than expected. While the report shared by Com2uS stated that the anime adaptation of ORV was slated for 2028, it hasn’t been officially confirmed by major distributors or production partners, leaving its status uncertain for now.

The anime was officially announced on July 7, 2024, at the Crunchyroll Industry Panel, which means the streaming platform for the anime has already been decided. ORV is expected to be a major hit after the anime debut, especially since it shares the same system trope, similar to the beloved action series,  Solo Leveling .

articles.title: Is the American Psycho Movie Remake Still Happening? Director Luca Guadagnino Just Gave a Disappointing Update
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Lionsgate There have been rumors of an American Psycho remake coming, but according to director Luca Guadagnino, it's not happening. Scott Z. Burns was attached to write the movie as far back as 2024, and Guadagnino was in talks to direct it at the time. The original American Psycho was released in 2000, directed by Mary […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There have been rumors of an American Psycho remake coming, but according to director Luca Guadagnino, it's not happening. Scott Z. Burns was attached to write the movie as far back as 2024, and Guadagnino was in talks to direct it at the time. The original American Psycho was released in 2000, directed by Mary Harron, wth Christian Bale starring as Patrick Bateman . Based on the novel by Bret Easton Ellis, the movie follows a yuppie in the 1980s who might or might not be a serial killer. In the end, the book and the movie adapted from it were actually an indictment of the yuppie lifestyle and consumerism that was prevalent in the 1980s. That made it a perfect movie for Guadagnino.

However, Guadagnino was on Deadline 's Crew Call podcast with Anthony D’Alessandro, and he was asked about the American Psycho remake. The director said, "Scott Z. Burns wrote a fantastic script. Unfortunately for me, as we speak, it’s not happening." He didn't elaborate any further on what was happening with the project.

The novel was considered to be unfilmable before Mary Harron adapted it, and what resulted was a cult classic that offered fans a look at Christian Bale before he took on the role of Bruce Wayne, in a film that proved he could play the role. Making a remake seemed almost as unlikely as turning the Ellis book into a movie in the first place. Bale was perfect as Patrick Bateman, and Harron did a spectacular job of creating a movie that left viewers wondering if what they just watched was real or all in the mind of Patrick Bateman. It would be hard to pull that off again, but if anyone could, it is Guadagnino.

Luca Guadagnino has made his name with some bizarre and offbeat movies, especially as he started to gain more attention in North America. He already took on a risky remake with his 2018 release of Suspiria, and his later films, including Bones and All , Challengers , and Artificial , showed that he could take familiar genres and make something completely different out of them. He could easily take something like American Psycho and make it his own.

Lionsgate was the one that reached out to Guadagnino, and the studio hasn't made any comment about the movie no longer being in development. While the director didn't say much about it, his comments that the movie is not happening make it sound like he didn't just leave the role as director, but that the entire remake is off the table right now. Lionsgate has continued to hold the rights since the original movie and was considering a television series in 2013 alongside FX, something else that never came to pass.

After 26 years, the only thing that has come close to a return to the world of American Psycho was the 2002 movie The Rules of Attraction , which starred James Van Der Beek as Sean Bateman, Patrick's brother. That movie was also based on an Ellis novel. There was also a maligned sequel that was originally a script called The Girl Who Wouldn't Die , but it was rewritten to make it a sequel to capitalize on the original film's popularity.

articles.title: 33 Years Later, This Bill Murray Masterpiece Is a Free to Stream Hit…Again
articles.summary: Courtesy of Columbia Pictures There are some movies that are made to be watched again and again…and again. That is particularly true of movies featuring time-travel and time-loops. In 1993, Bill Murray starred in one such movie that has the theme of repetition down to a fine art, where he played Phil Connors, a self-interested, cynical TV weatherman who […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There are some movies that are made to be watched again and again …and again. That is particularly true of movies featuring time-travel and time-loops. In 1993, Bill Murray starred in one such movie that has the theme of repetition down to a fine art, where he played Phil Connors, a self-interested, cynical TV weatherman who discovers that sometimes you have to get things wrong a lot before you finally find the path you are meant to take. For him, all of this takes place on the same day as he finds himself caught in a time-loop that refuses to release him from living the same day repeatedly until he learns that the world does not revolve around him. Of course, the day he is stuck in is Groundhog Day , and the movie has found its way back into the Tubi streaming chart as a heartwarming, snow-covered film for the whole family to enjoy.

Under the direction of Murray's Ghostbusters costar Harold Ramis, Groundhog Day pairs Murray's narcissistic Phil with his TV producer coworker, Rita, played by Andie MacDowell. The movie is basically about Phil proving that he can love someone other than himself while being driven to madness in his attempts to break out of the loop he has found himself in. Unfortunately, his efforts don't instantly help him free himself from his curse, but naturally things all work out in the end. Murray was riding high at the time of Groundhog Day , and it became one of his highest-rated movies, still holding a 93% Rotten Tomatoes audience score. The popularity of the actor, along with the nostalgic feelings that a three-decade-ols movie brings has made sure that Groundhog Day is never far away from another watch, and there is no better time to revisit it than when it is available on free streaming.

Groundhog Day is a movie that plays its story perfectly with Ramis' direction and Murray's impeccable comic timing making the movie a timeless classic that doesn't miss a beat as it balances its humor and heart. Yet there could have been many other ways the movie could have turned out differently. Murray was not first choice for the role, as others such as Tom Hanks, Michael Keaton and Kevin Cline were all in the mix, with Keaton actually turning down the role because he didn't understand the story. Additionally, the studio wanted the reason why Phil ends up caught in his time-loop explaining in the movie. Ideas floated included a lover's curse and a science experiment gone wrong, but thanks to Ramis and producer Trevor Albert scheduling those scenes too late to be filmed, the movie had to go ahead without them - for the better.

Despite behind-the-scenes conflicts between Ramis and a mid-divorce Murray, and Murray's original claims that he hated the movie, years later he would admit that he felt it was one of his best performances and one of Ramis' best directorial efforts. That is something that almost everyone agrees with, as Murray's grumpy portrayal of Phil - partly enhanced by the personal issues he was facing at the time - is what elevates the film beyond just a run of the mill comedy. In 2006, Groundhog Day was preserved in the US National Film Registry, and its time-loop scenario is one that has often been repeated but very rarely bettered . Do yourself a favor and watch Groundhog Day while it is available to stream for free on Tubi among your festive holiday movies.

Is Groundhog Day one of Bill Murray's most rewatchable movies? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Doctor Doom's Attempt to Change Hell Has Created a Whole New Nightmare for an Unexpected Hero
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Doctor Doom took control of Hell and claimed the throne that Mephisto once held in the pages of Captain America comics. While Doom is a terrifying villain, he has almost always been a just ruler, and he wanted to do the same thing to the demons and beings who called Hell their home. As a […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Doctor Doom took control of Hell and claimed the throne that Mephisto once held in the pages of Captain America comics. While Doom is a terrifying villain, he has almost always been a just ruler, and he wanted to do the same thing to the demons and beings who called Hell their home. As a result, he decided that it would be a good thing to make every contract that Mephisto made with humans null and void. He also agreed to let anyone who lived in Hell leave if they so desired, and he didn't seem to care where they went. This has caused untold problems in the Marvel Universe.

The most obvious problem has come in the pages of The Avengers , where murderous angel-like creatures have shown up to kill or capture anyone who was part of a deal that Mephisto had previously made, including Aunt May . However, making Hell a place that was free for demons to leave has created new problems for Doctor Doom, and he has swept in the most unexpected heroes of all in the new Black Panther & Namor: Doomed miniseries by Ethan S. Parker, Griffin Sheridan, and Stefano Nesi.

No one could have expected Black Panther and Namor to team up to help Doctor Doom, but that is what has happened in this new miniseries. The reason for the reluctant team-up was simple. Demons attacked Atlantis, and they threatened to raid Wakanda next. The two bitter rivals agreed to team up to chase the demons back to Hell, which is when they realized that Doctor Doom was the new ruler there. While Doom seemed like their new common enemy, they quickly learned that it wasn't Doctor Doom who sent the demons, but a new threat known as the Kingkiller. Not only were Namor and Black Panther targeted, but so was Star-Lord, the crowned head of the Galactic Union. This Kingkiller is attacking kings all over the universe.

In Hell, Doctor Doom explained that the Kingkiller is the same species as the Watchers, which means she borders on all-powerful, but her motives are unclear. While they had a common enemy to fight, the biggest problem is that Doctor Doom, Namor, and Black Panther all hate each other, and none of them really want to work with the others. However, it was Doom who was the voice of reason, telling the two kings to stand by him in this fight or return to die with their kingdoms. It also showed that Doom knew he wasn't strong enough to win this battle on his own. But at the same time, he was the one who caused this.

Doctor Doom immediately wanted to improve on what Mephisto had done before, and the only reason was to prove he was the better ruler in Hell. When he voided all the deals and allowed any demon who didn't want to live there to leave, he thought he was proving himself a good king to the citizens of the underworld. But he did this based on vanity, and he never considered, or cared about, what would happen next. Clearly, Doom didn't care if the demons wreaked havoc on other realms, even if that was Earth. As always, he only cared about his own people. But as he said in this issue, he didn't foresee a plan brewing in Hell after he freed all the captive souls from Hell.

Even Namor called out Doom for his short-sighted and arrogant actions. What was shocking was when Black Panther stood up for Doom and said that the freedom of the citizens of Hell was all that Doom should care about, even in the face of the destruction that Atlantis faced. However, Black Panther did admit that Doom would answer for all his crimes. But none of that matters right now, because it is Doctor Doom's actions that have put Earth in danger with the broken pacts, and now the entire universe is in danger from a villain who lives deep in a pocket dimension in Hell.

By the end of Black Panther & Namor: Doomed #3, Namor ended up separated from the other two and faced a being who died fighting to defend Atlantis. He then met up with the Kingkiller, who showed him why so many had to die, and that was the cliffhanger for this month's issue. This series is yet another example of why Doctor Doom, no matter where he is, can cause the most problems for all of Earth's heroes, even those as diametrically opposed as Black Panther and Namor.

Luna played Robbie Reyes' version of the Ghost Rider in Marvel's Agents of SHIELD Season 4. He appeared in 10 episodes that season, but that was the last anyone had seen of the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Former Ghost Rider actor Gabriel Luna has said he has changed his stance on a possible return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Luna played Robbie Reyes' version of the Ghost Rider in Marvel's Agents of SHIELD Season 4. He appeared in 10 episodes that season, but that was the last anyone had seen of the character in the MCU. He was supposed to get his own streaming series when Hulu was working on creating a series of shows set in the dark corners of Marvel, but the only show that was made and released was Helstrom. As for Luna, it seemed his time as Ghost Rider had come to an end.

Luna had previously said he wasn't planning on returning to the MCU as Ghost Rider, but he said that he changed his mind in a recent interview. "Years ago, my stock answer to this question was that I was so proud of what we did with Agents of SHIELD and with Robbie Reyes that to continue it would only give me the potential or the opportunity to tarnish it," Luna told The Hollywood Reporter . "But as the multiverse started to take shape within the films and the questions started to be asked at a higher clip, I eventually had to pivot in my stance. I now think that there is potential, and I’m absolutely open to it."

Robbie Reyes Would Be a Great Addition to the MCU Image Courtesy of Marvel There have been some unsubstantiated rumors that Robbie Reyes' Ghost Rider was under consideration to return to the MCU as part of the next Avengers lineup. While Luna was never mentioned, and he might be a little too old for the character now, he could be a nice addition. Those rumors claimed that the next Avengers team could also feature names like She-Hulk and a recast Iron Man. The lineup is almost the exact same one from the 2018 Jason Aaron Avengers comic book run, which featured the team facing the Celestials. Since the Celestials are part of an MCU storyline from Eternals that hasn't been completed, it makes sense.

Now, this was just a rumor, and there is no evidence for it other than scoopers throwing the names out there. This could possibly be nothing more than an inspiration for how the next Avengers team could look in the post- Secret Wars world. More interestingly, bringing in Robbie Reyes for a Midnight Sons movie and having two possible Ghost Riders working either together or against each other could be an even more interesting proposition. Past Midnight Sons comics have featured multiple Ghost Riders , often at the same time. Robbie Reyes brings something that Johnny Blaze doesn't, and there is room in the MCU for both of them.

Luna did mention in the interview that the MCU would need to age the character up for this to work if he plays Robbie Reyes again. He mentioned that it could allow him to mature more and evolve from where he was on Marvel's Agents of SHIELD . As for why he has changed his mind, Luna said that he did a 10-year anniversary celebration, and when he saw how much the fans still love Robbie Reyes , he changed his mind and is open to the return. "I’ve maintained my health and my agility," Luna said. "My physical prowess has always been a strength of what I do, and so I’m still there in mind and body. I’m totally down."

articles.title: Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando Are Married
articles.summary: The couple began dating in 2021 after meeting on a blind date.
articles.content:
Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando are married.

articles.title: This Rare Mego Star Trek Toy Wasn't Based on Any Episode, But It Captured Everything That Made the Line Special
articles.summary: Mego’s Star Trek line is synonymous with its iconic Enterprise Bridge playset. Less discussed is the even more elaborate, impressive playset that Mego released as a follow-up in 1976, finally giving kids a place to send the figures they put through the Enterprise’s transporter: the “Mission to Gamma VI.” Standing at over eighteen inches tall, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Mego’s Star Trek line is synonymous with its iconic Enterprise Bridge playset . Less discussed is the even more elaborate, impressive playset that Mego released as a follow-up in 1976, finally giving kids a place to send the figures they put through the Enterprise’s transporter: the “Mission to Gamma VI.” Standing at over eighteen inches tall, the playset gave kids an exotic alien world for the Enterprise crew to explore. Gamma VI was a fully-rendered alien ecosystem, with the set’s accessories and action features representing three different species that inhabited the strange new world. It’s these bizarre action features that serve as the set’s claim to fame today: while Mego took some creative liberties with its Enterprise, they took far more with the “Mission to Gamma VI.” Gamma VI was virtually an original creation, its central stone-faced idol bearing a cursory resemblance to the one seen in season two episode “The Apple.”

There’s another critical difference between the Mego Enterprise Bridge and the “Mission to Gamma VI:” rarity. While the Enterprise was the top-selling toy of 1975, the “Mission to Gamma VI” scarcely reached retail shelves – owing in part to the box’s massive footprint – making it the single rarest and most sought-after release in Mego’s Star Trek line. Playsets are one of the challenges of Mego’s eight-inch action figures, demonstrated in sets like “Mission to Gamma VI” and the World’s Greatest Super-Heroes Wayne Foundation . To scale with Mego figures, these sets had to tower, making a significant investment of space for retailers and parents alike. Loose, complete samples of the set sell for up to $1k, with many of its action-features and accessories easily lost, damaged, or ruined by play. Boxed samples can sell for more than double that. The only sample currently on eBay sits at a buy-it-now asking price of $2.5k , owing to its incredibly rare sealed-in-box condition.

Beaming down to Gamma VI, Mego’s Enterprise crew would be met with a rocky, desolate planet surface represented through a cardboard baseplate. The only sign of life is a plastic plant, whose articulated leaves could be used to trap the unwary crewman who steps too close. The dominant feature of Gamma VI’s landscape, however, was the imposing stone face carved into a jagged cliffside. This is the aspect of the playset that bears the closest resemblance to the source material, seemingly modeled loosely off of the “Vaal” statue from the aforementioned episode “The Apple.” Given Mego’s penchant for loose adaptations of its Star Trek aliens , it feels reasonable to call Vaal the basis for “Mission to Gamma VI” – especially given that “Gamma Trianguli VI” is the name of the planet in “The Apple.”

The lizard-like face looms over a stepped platform, looking almost like a sacrificial altar. Looking closer, one would expect to find a door in the carved stone wall. Instead, kids can push the platform and release a trap door, sending their Captain Kirk or Mister Spock tumbling into the temple’s interior. From there, they can explore the secrets of Gamma VI’s temple, less detailed but just as fun as the exterior. The inside is functionally a cave, given two levels of play by a cardboard structure. More play features round out the exterior, including a movable jaw and glow-in-the-dark eyes on the “Vaal” stone face; as well as two other native alien species. A textured green glove fits through a hole in the playset, letting kids become what the box calls the “Cave Glove Creature,” pictured there snatching an unsuspecting Spock. Additionally, the set included four weird, two-inch tall aliens, sculpted to cling to jutting spikes along the plastic wall. These don’t have any basis in the series, and the difference in scale makes it a bit difficult to have them interact with other figures.

It’s been said that Star Trek toys have almost never really been for kids: whether it was Galoob’s 1987 Star Trek: The Next Generation line, or Playmates’ epic 1990s Star Trek figures, the primary target audience was adult collectors. Catering to these adult collectors, these lines ensured their figures, characters, and accessories were coming straight from the source material. Playmates’ line especially, with its mail-away figures, ToyFare magazine exclusives, and limited-edition chases, were designed to engage grown-up Trekkies with the time and budget to obsess over the line. Mego’s line came at a completely different point in toy history, inspired directly by the overwhelming popularity of early-seventies Star Trek reruns with children. While Playmates or Galoob’s figures were collectors’ items as much as toys, Mego’s garish, pastel-colored Star Trek was firmly intended for kids.

Mego’s Star Trek line came at a time when the first and only consideration for toys was whether they would appeal to kids. Mego wasn’t beholden to screen accuracy, they were beholden to playaiblity. Designing their “Mission to Gamma VI,” the first and only question was if it would hold the interest of a child. As illustrated by the previous section, it absolutely woud: Mego designed its play features to gradually reveal themselves, playing out in a structure like an episode of Star Trek . A kid sitting down with the set and their Enterprise crew was exploring an alien planet with them, and imagining in real-time how their heroes would respond to the sudden dangers and developments posed by Gamma VI’s flora and fauna. Though it barely resembled the episode of Star Trek that it was based on, the “Mission to Gamma VI” embodied the spirit of the series perfectly, encouraging exploration, discovery, and a sense of adventure.

articles.title: 3 Female Anime Leads of 2026 Who Are Breaking the Male-Dominated Industry
articles.summary: The anime industry has arguably long been accused of being male-dominated, largely thanks to the success of numerous shonen anime that established the boy-oriented genre as a leading force in entertainment. However, while it has taken decades longer than other mediums, the anime industry is also evolving and embracing more modern elements, including female leads […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The anime industry has arguably long been accused of being male-dominated, largely thanks to the success of numerous shonen anime that established the boy-oriented genre as a leading force in entertainment. However, while it has taken decades longer than other mediums, the anime industry is also evolving and embracing more modern elements, including female leads taking center stage.

The year 2026 has been particularly notable in this regard, witnessing the emergence of several series featuring female leads, including masterpieces created by female authors. However, it is the female protagonists themselves who have made an epic impact, breaking the mold of a traditionally male-dominated industry. These three leads, each showcasing a different kind of strength and variety, prove just that.

Yamada from Smoking Behind the Supermarket with You is the type of lead who rarely gets the spotlight. However, this anime proves that a laid-back yet demure female protagonist can work just as well. At the supermarket, Yamada is the sweet cashier whom Sasaki puts on a pedestal. However, her alternate personality, complete with a leather jacket and piercings, showcases an unmatched sense of coolness. In both aspects, she is a character who supports the male lead through her subtle gestures. However, that doesn't mean she exists solely for Sasaki's sake.

Yamada's entire character feels incredibly real, as she deals with the everyday struggles one would expect from an ordinary person. Her support for Sasaki as Tayama, and the way she receives the same support in return, create a back-and-forth dynamic that feels genuine and soothing. In essence, her role as a female lead brings a sense of realism to the anime industry and broadens its horizons in a way that is very much needed.

The magical seinen series Witch Hat Atelier challenges the notion that magical stories featuring witches are catered exclusively towards female audiences, or that witches only exist to amplify the presence of wizards. The series does this by presenting Coco as a compelling protagonist, with her love and curiosity for magic serving as the driving force behind her journey, which is filled with darkness and obstacles. What makes Coco such a delight to watch is her unwavering resolve to never give up and overcome every challenge.

This notion was previously dominated by male protagonists in the anime industry, who constantly embodied the never-give-up spirit, while female characters were often relegated to supporting roles. However, Coco fully embodies this aspect, presenting the famous never-give-up spirit and carrying the story into a new age, arguably better than most shonen anime protagonists of 2026. In doing so, she makes one of the strongest impacts on the traditionally male-dominated industry.

Women in political environments, even today in real life, are often frowned upon, and anime has followed this pattern for decades. This is what makes Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia such a refreshing series, as its entire premise revolves around a political revenge plot led by a female character, Sitara, who begins as a slave before setting her sights on the entire Mongol Empire. The series establishes this through Sitara's experience of witnessing the death of her beloved family, who gave her everything despite their circumstances as slaves.

Swearing revenge on the Mongol Empire, whose tyranny was responsible for her family's suffering, Sitara begins playing a political game with the aim of overthrowing the empire from within. However, that is easier said than done, and Sitara continues to face new challenges. It is astonishing to see her overcome each obstacle while remaining committed to her revenge, all while befriending another female character who becomes just as fascinating a lead as Sitara herself. Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia is truly one of the most revolutionary anime of 2026 , proving through its female leads that women can take center stage and challenge the traditionally male-dominated anime industry.

articles.title: A Cancelled Comic Ended Up One of the Most Important Issues in Marvel History All Because of One Character
articles.summary: It is hard to imagine the world of entertainment without Marvel. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It is hard to imagine the world of entertainment without Marvel. That is especially true right now as we get ready for the arrival of Avengers: Doomsday in theaters in just over a month, but while the MCU is huge, Marvel is bigger than the movies. It’s the comics that is the true driving force behind the entertainment giant as, without the stories across the pages of Marvel Comics , there’d be no MCU because without the comics there would be no Iron Man, no Captain America, no Hulk, no Spider-Man — you get the idea. And while it’s hard to imagine entertainment without Marvel, it’s also hard to imagine Marvel without one of its most beloved characters, and it is a character that we almost didn’t get because of a book that almost didn’t happen but ended up changing everything.

Every comic book fan knows that Spider-Man’s first appearance was in Amazing Fantasy #15 in August 1962. The webslinger, created by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko was an instant hit and has gone on to be one of the most popular and profitable characters not only in Marvel Comics but in comics generally since. But what many don’t realize is that Spider-Man almost didn’t happen, that his debut came with the final issue of an anthology series and everyone expected the character to fail right along with the book — except it didn’t.

Amazing Fantasy itself has an interesting history, having started in 1961 as Amazing Adventures , but by issue #7 it had become Amazing Adult Fantas y and was an anthology book geared towards adults with short, science fiction stories and a tagline of “the magazine that respects your intelligence.” While the idea was interesting — a book tailored to the adult reader — it didn’t do well. Sales were poor and then-publisher Martin Goodman made the call to cancel the title with issue #15. Of course, Amazing Adult Fantasy coming to an end presented a different opportunity that would end up changing Marvel forever.

At the same time Amazing Adult Fantasy was faltering, as the story goes Lee was looking to introduce a completely different type of superhero, one that would appeal to a younger audience. At this point in comics, all of the heroes were adults and any teen characters were sidekicks. The character envisioned for this would be different, a regular teen with actual real-world issues and challenges: an everyday hero. It wasn’t an idea that got a lot of traction with the powers that be, but with Amazing Adult Fantasy dying, there was an opportunity. The final issue was rebranded as Amazing Fantasy , Spider-Man got the cover and became the central hero, Ditko worked his artistic magic, and that was that. If it failed, at least they tried.

Amazing Fantasy was indeed properly cancelled, but when sales figures rolled in what had been a dying book turned out to be a huge hit. The book was one of the year’s best sellers and immediately, Spider-Man got his own book , The Amazing Spider-Man #1 and it’s a book that continues even today. Spider-Man himself has gone on to be one of the most famous and beloved characters in all of comics and is easily Marvel’s biggest and most popular. Granted, Peter Parker/Spider-Man has been through a number of shifts and changes over the years and he’s not exactly the teen hero anymore, but he is still very much the everyday hero. Spider-Man is the hero that anyone can see themself in. He has real world problems in addition to taking on wild villains and crazy threats. He is, in many ways, the most human of superheroes.

It’s also just fascinating that his origin comes from a combination of a failure and a “what’s the worst that could happen if we try” sort of situation. There’s something deeply relatable about that. How often do we as people find ourselves with our backs to the wall, in situations where all hope seems lost and we are down to trying just one more thing and if we fail, well, at least we tried? The fact that one of our greatest fictional characters has that as his publication origin story makes him even more endearing.

Wild how something that almost didn’t happen ended up changing everything, but boy are we glad it did.

What do you think about the wild story of how a cancelled comic led to Spider-Man? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Star-Lord's First Appearance Is Hiding in This 1976 Marvel Comic, and He's Nothing Like the MCU Hero
articles.summary: James Gunn and Guardians of the Galaxy changed the landscape of the MCU in 2014. While The Avengers were a bunch of big egos that came together to save Earth, The Guardians were an unruly bunch of misfits that could barely work together to save a PDF file. The movie perfectly illustrated this through its […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google James Gunn and Guardians of the Galaxy changed the landscape of the MCU in 2014. While The Avengers were a bunch of big egos that came together to save Earth, The Guardians were an unruly bunch of misfits that could barely work together to save a PDF file. The movie perfectly illustrated this through its hilarious writing, with each character having their share of issues and quirks. It essentially brought humor to the MCU. However, things were not always like that, especially for the team's leader, Star Lord. 1976's Marvel Preview #4 Star-Lord featured his first appearance, and is currently up for auction at Heritage . Unlike the funny and cocky Peter Quill we know and love today, this one was on a path of vengeance.

While this is Star Lord's first ever appearance, it's technically not his comic book debut, as Marvel Preview was a magazine that gave readers a taste of the publisher's upcoming comics. Peter was born to Meredith Quill in Ohio, but his father knew that he biologically belonged to an alien being. That's about the only similarity with the modern version of the hero, as his original backstory was way more tragic. Enraged with suspicion, Meredith's husband Jake tried to kill Peter as a baby, but suffered a mysterious heart attack. Then, as a kid Peter witnessed aliens murdering his mother, after which he became an angry and distant person, focused only on vengeance. After making it as an astronaut, he injured his fellow crewmates and approached the mysterious Master of the Sun, who gave him the powers of Star Lord and a gun that could control earth, fire, wind, and water. That's not the Star Lord we know today.

When we think of Star Lord, we imagine Chris Pratt singing '80s hits while saying something stupid to Gamora, Rocket, or Drax. And let's face it, The Guardians of the Galaxy weren't really that popular before their MCU appearance. However, James Gunn's adaptation of the team and characters gave the cinematic universe a whole new angle, with stunning interstellar settings and a dysfunctional team with a laughable dynamic. It's a far cry from the this original version of Star Lord, who was a character with nothing but revenge on his mind. Thankfully, future comic issues, as well as the movies, decided to go with the modern rendition of the character.

Coming across a first-appearance comic is always amazing, especially if the character is nothing like how we know them today. Costumes have always changed over the years and personalities have evolved with the decades, but perhaps no well known comic book character has seen such a dramatic change as Star Lord. And that's what makes this issue even more special. But what's strange about this CGC NM+ 9.6 graded issue is that despite Star Lord's first appearance and its great condition, it's currently going for just $15. I know that's probably because it's a magazine and not a comic, but it's still one hell of a collectible for fans of Guardians of the Galaxy. Peter Quill has come a long way since his vengeance filled first appearance, and this collectible is a great testament to it.

Which other comic book characters were drastically different in their first appearances? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: Blake Shelton Loves Being A Stepdad To Gwen Stefani’s Kids, But What’s His ‘Most Cliche’ Dad Role?

articles.content:
Blake Shelton has never shied away from sharing lessons he’s learned from being the stepdad of Gwen Stefani’s kids. In fact, he’s been candid about realizing that he can be someone they can lean on . Now, he’s revealed the “most cliché” about him, and it’s both very sweet and shows how he and his wife's kids lean on and support each other.

When he was asked if he also gets on the trampoline, Shelton joked that “just throwing the ball wears [him] out.” There’s that signature humor we saw on The Voice coming out. However, overall, the singer was very clear that he loves doing this with his kid. And I really can’t think of anything more father-son coded than playing catch in the yard together. So, yes, while cliché, it’s incredibly sweet.

Shelton has always been very supportive of his stepson’s music career , and I love that they bond over it on a daily basis. I can’t help but wonder if they have a shared playlist and if the “God Gave Me You” singer’s love for country music has rubbed off on him.
