articles.title: Developer Warns Nintendo Fans Not to Buy Their Switch 2 Games
articles.summary: An independent developer has warned Nintendo fans, via Reddit, not to buy their new Nintendo Switch 2 games. Of course, there's a good reason. This warning is specifically for those who already own the Nintendo Switch versions of the games in question. While the developer is not prepared to offer free Switch 2 upgrades for […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google An independent developer has warned Nintendo fans, via Reddit, not to buy their new Nintendo Switch 2 games. Of course, there's a good reason. This warning is specifically for those who already own the Nintendo Switch versions of the games in question. While the developer is not prepared to offer free Switch 2 upgrades for owners of the Switch versions, they will be offering those who own the Switch versions 80% off the Nintendo Switch 2 versions. That said, due to processing times, this offer won't take effect until after November 21 in North America and until after November 28th in Europe, Australia, and New Zealand.

Using the Nintendo Switch 2 Reddit page, developer Bedtime Digital Games has specifically relayed the above information about the new Nintendo Switch 2 version of Figment and its sequel, Figment 2: Creed Valley . The developer also relayed this information via Nintendo's built-in news and announcement system, but the developer is doubtful that many check those messages; hence the post on the Switch 2 Reddit page.

"We are really sorry if this impacted you. We want you to have the discount, and we're super grateful for the support you've shown our indie studio over the years," writes Bedtime Digital Games to the Nintendo Switch 2 Reddit page.

Nintendo Fans Appreciate the Honesty As you would expect, Nintendo fans were very receptive to the warning, which shot to the top of the Switch 2 Reddit page.

"I respect the hell out of this. Congrats on the launch," reads one of the top comments. Another adds, "Dudes this game wasn’t even on my radar, but this just bought you a purchase. I respect this so damn much. In a world filled with money-hungry companies, this is a breath of fresh air."

For the games themselves — for those unfamiliar like the commentator above — they are surreal action-adventure games. The first game debuted in 2017 to a 77 on Metacritic and positive user reviews, as evidenced by its 88% approval rating on Steam. The sequel followed six years later in 2023, releasing to a similar 76 on Metacritic and a 94% approval rating on Steam. The first game costs $20, while the sequel runs at $25.

According to the trailer above, the pair of games have combined for over a million sales on the Nintendo Switch alone, so there are likely many Switch 2 users this warning is relevant to. The new Nintendo Switch 2 versions most notably include a performance upgrade to 60 FPS, alongside visual upgrades as well. Loading times are also substantially faster. What there isn't is new content.

Those hoping and on the lookout for free Nintendo Switch 2 upgrades will be happy to know there are some of those as well. To this end, three different free Nintendo Switch 2 upgrades were all recently released at once.

articles.title: Every Known Ending of GTA 6 Explained, & How To Unlock Each of Them
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games The roller coaster ride of a campaign in Grand Theft Auto 6 ends depending on your actions, with six different endings that can come up based on your choices. Having a criminal profile, a stable relationship, or even stored money amounts can make the credits come from different places, adding to the insanely deep details […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The roller coaster ride of a campaign in Grand Theft Auto 6 ends depending on your actions, with six different endings that can come up based on your choices. Having a criminal profile, a stable relationship, or even stored money amounts can make the credits come from different places, adding to the insanely deep details of Rockstar's latest hit . The way in which you handle the last mission can also lead you to a unique fate, with several key decisions being tied to the direction Jason and Lucia's lives will go.

Before you reach an ending in GTA 6 , you first have to make a choice regarding Mendez in the final chapter of the game, as taking his deal or shooting him leads to different outcomes. Siding with Mendez leads to a completely different final act compared to if you shoot him, creating multiple scenarios that could be both good or disastrous for each main character. This is perhaps the biggest choice in the game for that reason, but many other factors contribute to what outcome you eventually do get by the time credits roll.

Once you go past the point of no return in GTA 6 , the first major ending comes from taking Mendez's deal after Lucia breaks out Jason from a police precinct. However, it's hard to tell when you can make the deal at first, as the game will only offer an option to shoot Mendez after confronting him outside the building. By choosing not to shoot, a new "Take Deal" prompt will come up, which changes that last section of GTA 6 from what most players encounter. In a way, this is the secret route most players will miss, rather than the Bonny and Clyde-style bridge finale that is more common.

Choosing to partner up with Mendez takes Jason and Lucia to The Tower finale instead, where a group of cops ambush both characters to get a set of government files. These files are tied to Jason and Lucia's freedom, but players have the option to keep going along with their Mendez partnership in this moment. Choosing to do so gets both characters put in handcuffs for "optics" according to Mendez, before Mendez drives away with the two in the back of his car. A haunting cutscene takes place here, where Mendez says he's taking Jason and Lucia "where they need to go."

This is by far the worst ending in GTA 6 , as Mendez drives into the swampy regions of Leonida before credits roll. The aftermath of this shows Mendez getting promoted and the protagonists' kid being orphaned, but there's no sign of Jason or Lucia. It is revealed in the last shot that Jason and Lucia were shot and killed by Mendez, before their bodies were dumped in the swamps. A final image of Jason and Lucia's skulls near an alligator someplace in the middle of nowhere wetlands is haunting, hinting that Mendez simply left them to rot after getting what he wanted.

If you don't trust Mendez and try to fight your way out of the police ambush after taking his deal initially, you'll be locked into the endings tied to The Tower finale of GTA 6 . Technically, there are two endings here rather than one, giving GTA 6 seven possible endings instead of six. That being said, all endings tied to The Tower mission are not affected by in-game factors like some others are, as you don't have a strong romance or weak criminal presence to reach The Tower's outcomes. Out of the two endings here, your options are the following:

The last cutscene of this ending depends on your choice, with a "bad" ending coming from having Lucia fight back with Jason to defend him, while the other choice leads to a somewhat "neutral" conclusion. Escaping Giorgio's shootout and making it to the Tower roof leads to this decision coming up, with Jason saying that he doesn't want to spend 25 years in a cage. Honoring Jason's sacrifice here as Lucia by staying down allows her to make a government deal, leading to her being free and able to see her son.

The reason this ending is more "neutral" than good isn't just due to Jason dying through his sacrifice. During the ending, despite Lucia being able to get back to her son, the lack of support Lucia has (through in-game money amounts) prevent her from being able to raise her son on her own. As a result, a cutscene shows her still owning a gun and pulling up to a store to rob it, mirroring the beginning sections of GTA 6 in a sad, full-circle moment. As of this time is writing, it is unknown if other actions change this ending, such as a stronger romantic bond between Jason and Lucia or having more money stored in a BuckMe account.

The most common endings in GTA 6 appear when you choose to shoot Mendez rather than take any sort of deal with him. This leads to the "End of the Road" final mission, where Jason and Lucia are driving away from the cops after being warned about an ambush ahead of time. Yet, this doesn't prevent them from reaching a blockade of officers on a secluded bridge, where players' choices all culminate into a series of options leading to four different endings. The two decisions given to you are to "Swim for It" or "No Surrender," with the latter being the quickest.

Choosing not to surrender to the cops has Jason and Lucia decide to "just keep going," and have a final shootout with the authorities. Whether you choose to stand and fight or try to forcibly drive through enemy forces, this is an unwinnable encounter, leading to Jason and Lucia's deaths regardless of what you do. If you have at least $2.5 million saved in a BuckMe family account, Jason and Lucia's kid will have a better chance at a supported life, but the final cutscenes will still show a life without his parents. A final scene shows a framed picture of Jason or Lucia, indicating one of the game's bad endings.

While a Bonnie and Clyde blaze of glory has a poetic ring to it, a less violent solution to the Bridge encounter is picking "Swim for It," with Jason suggesting jumping off the bridge and swimming away from the police. This is where GTA 6 will evaluate your choices up until this point, taking into account how close Jason and Lucia are to one another and how much money you have stored up. If Jason and Lucia's relationship in GTA 6 has reached the max value of "Hot Together," this option should show up as a possibility. However, the other factor to get this ending to work depends on your criminal profile.

Should either Jason or Lucia be considered a "Psycho" or "Irredeemable" criminal through their criminal profile, one character will attempt to exist the car to surrender, but still hold onto a gun. This alerts the trigger-happy police, who gun down both characters in the car, once again leading to a bad ending. Being a smarter criminal throughout the game can lower your wanted status to prevent this, so keeping a low profile may be the only way to avoid this ending. Just like the No Surrender ending, the final cutscenes with this one show an orphaned son whose life depends on your saved money.

The good endings to GTA 6 come from the results of the "Swim for It" choice that are backed up by your other decisions within the game. If your criminal profile isn't too high, Jason will exit the car on the bridge without a gun, allowing Lucia to do the same. Doing this lets both characters reach the edge of the bridge, where they both plan to jump off. That being said, Jason stays behind while Lucia falls, giving her time and a distraction to escape while he gets arrested. This is partially due to the government deal regarding the aforementioned file, with the deal itself really only applying to Lucia.

This ending does give Jason and Lucia a way for both of them to live, albeit with Jason in prison. Lucia is able to make the deal involving the file and get to her son, without the added pressure of instability seen in the Tower ending. During this part of GTA 6 , the last cutscene shows Jason being visited by Lucia and the couple's son, with the added hope of Jason perhaps being able to get out of prison one day. While slightly bittersweet, it is an ending with more hope than many of the others.

The "true" ending to GTA 6 comes from the same choices as the last one, but only when you have the following three criteria filled out:

Having all of these milestones will change the ending cutscenes after Jason takes the fall for Lucia after choosing the "Swim for It" option at the bridge. Jason still goes to jail and Lucia is able to make the government deal, but now the BuckMe money is successfully transferred to Lucia in the process. This does take two years, yet it gives Lucia the chance to pay off Jason's bail, letting him walk free early from prison. This ending sees Lucia and Jason reunite outside of jail with their son, in a final shot that shows that all the strife was finally worth it. Among all the possible endings, this one is clearly the best players can get.

Rockstar has teased that there might be even more undiscovered endings to the game players haven't figured out yet, possibly influenced by other actions taken until the finale. The extensive detail tied to the known conclusions are already layered, so it wouldn't be surprising to see one or two new endings come up as players continue to explore Rockstar's latest title. For now, GTA 6 's endings are heavily dependent on player actions, reflecting the immersive quality of the game that is earning it so much praise.

What is the ending you want to see the most in GTA 6 ? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: Dwayne Johnson's Divisive Record-Breaking Action Adventure Is Flying Up the Streaming Charts 2 Years Later
articles.summary: Courtesy of Amazon MGM Studios Although there are always people who like to smell what The Rock is cooking, the number who enjoy dining on the movies served up by Dwayne Johnson in cinemas is a finite one. Despite appearing in massive franchise movies like The Fast and the Furious and Jumanji, when Johnson is the lead in his own […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Although there are always people who like to smell what The Rock is cooking, the number who enjoy dining on the movies served up by Dwayne Johnson in cinemas is a finite one. Despite appearing in massive franchise movies like The Fast and the Furious and Jumanji , when Johnson is the lead in his own film, success is not always guaranteed despite the wrestler-turned-actor's tireless work to promote the movies he appears in. In 2024, Johnson teamed up with Marvel favorites Chris Evans and J.K. Simmons for a festive movie that promised big action, big laughs and little need to exert brain cells. Released on Prime Video after a disappointing theatrical run, Red One became a record-breaking streaming success as the platform's most watched movie of all time. Two years later, it is now heading back up the charts as fans start to work their way through Christmas movie playlists to get in the holiday mood.

Following the success of Johnson's Jumanji sequels - the third and final of which is about to hit cinemas soon - director Jake Kasden was the perfect person to bring Johnson's brand of over-the-top action to a festive setting. The story focuses on Callum Drift, Johnson's head of North Pole security who finds his retirement plans in jeopardy when Santa (a bizarrely ripped Simmons) is kidnapped. Enlisting the help of bounty hunter and black-hat hacker Jack O'Malley (Evans), the mission to save the man in the red suit turns into a globe-trotting adventure yarn that is just a religious artefact away from being an Indiana Jones pastiche. As the type of throwaway big and loud action movie Johnson has excelled at for more than quarter of a century, the film was much more pleasing to audiences than critics, and its record-breaking stats prove it.

In the last several years, the boom in streaming and shorter release windows between cinema debut and home release has changed the way many people now choose to watch movies. Where there used to be six to eight month wait to see a movie at home, that has now been reduced to six to eight weeks, or even less in many cases. This means that most people don't feel they are missing out if they aren't able to catch the latest blockbuster in cinemas. Red One was exactly the kind of movie that was impacted by this. Having originally being planned as a streaming exclusive, the film was released in cinemas on November 6, just over a month before it then hit Prime Video on December 12. With a mega $250 million budget, the $185.6 million worldwide gross would have been seen as a huge flop several years earlier.

However, that was just a taster for the main course, as Red One blasted onto Prime Video with a record-breaking 50 million viewers in the first four days. That is a story that has played out several times in the last few years, with cinematic flops becoming huge attractions to streaming audiences. This year's Masters of the Universe, another Amazon-made movie, brought in a massive streaming audience compared to its lacking box office result earlier in the year. For many studios, cinema box office results are only one half of the story for any release now, and for a movie like Red One , with its Christmas aesthetic, the already bulging sack of views from the past two years will only grow every time the holiday season comes around . This will certainly make up for any disappointment about its original theatrical haul.

Is Red One on your Christmas movie list? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Percy Jackson Has Been Making Percabeth A 'Slow Burn'. I’m Already Seeing It More In Season 3
articles.summary: Our demigod babies are growing up!
articles.content:
SPOILERS ahead for Percy Jackson and the Olympians' Season 3 two-episode premiere, now streaming for those with a Disney+ subscription or Hulu subscription .

The last time CinemaBlend caught up with the showrunners, they told us they’re trying to “slow burn” the relationship between Percy and Annabeth . When I caught up with them again, Jonathan E. Steinberg delved into where we’re at this season with their dynamic, saying this:

Oh, I feel it. I mean, what sticks out to me so far is that dance scene between them in Episode 1. After Percy famously told Annabeth he would “burn it all down” for her last season if he had to, you can feel this unsaid chemistry between them. However, in true teenage boy fashion, Percy shoots down the comment when Annabeth brings it up. Then, right before she gets captured by the manticore, Percy looks like he was about to risk everything to try to save her if Artemis didn’t pull him off the ledge.

Season 3 really feels like the sweet spot for Percy and the rest of the cast, where they are at the right age for the show to mature a bit more, and that makes me more excited for what’s to come. I know there’s always discourse around the book changes in TV shows like this, but I like what’s been done so far. For one, we’re getting to see Annabeth’s time in captivity, and we’re also getting more Percabeth moments ahead of the pair going from friends to romantic partners.

articles.title: What Inspired Glen Powell To Play A Country Singer? It Involves Shotgunning Beer With Luke Combs
articles.summary: Certainly not mad about seeing Glen Powell in a cowboy hat again.
articles.content:
We've seen Glen Powell chase tornadoes, fly airplanes and play a football player in disguise. Next, he'll be transforming into a country singer for The Comeback King , a comedy he's collaborating with Judd Apatow on that will premiere on the 2027 movie schedule in February. So, what inspired him to put the cowboy hat back on and sing? Well, it turns out Twisters and shotgunning a beer with Luke Combs had something to do with it.

I can’t say I blame the Hit Man actor for getting caught up in that moment with his fellow Twisters castmates and Luke Combs. Together, they all shotgunned beer on stage at Combs’ NYC concert back in the summer of 2024, and the video went viral on TikTok .

How Glen Powell was able to once again assemble the Avengers of country music, I’ll never know. But I’m super excited to see the likes of Miranda Lambert, Jelly Roll, Brad Paisley, and Shaboozey bring their A-game alongside Powell in this epic ensemble comedy when it premieres on February 5, 2027. While we wait for that, I think we should all say thank you to Luke Combs too for helping inspire this film that looks like it'll be a lot of country fun.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Marvel Comics was able to rise to the top of the superhero game by changing it. Go and read Fantastic Four #1 from 1961 and then read Justice League of America #21, from the same year. While they are both excellent comics, there's so much more heart and personality in Fantastic Four #1. At the time, that was revolutionary and it allowed the House of Ideas to become the stunning edifice it is today. Superhero comics have changed a lot over the years and as much as I love DC, even I have to admit that Marvel played a massive role in the evolution of the medium. Marvel is all about changing the game, with numerous reveals that set the comic industry on fire.

There's nothing like picking up a comic and getting a jaw-dropping moment. It gets even better when that jaw-dropping moment ripples outward, transforming everything it touches. Marvel's creators have mastered giving readers these kinds of amazing moments, with these five game-changing reveals rocking the Marvel Universe, including Wolverine's most shocking moment.

Captain America is Marvel's greatest soldier , having fought against evil in World War II and beyond. Cap was teamed up with Bucky, a garishly dressed young man with a smile on his face and a machine gun in his hand. Bucky'd end up dead by the end of the war, and his loss was one of the formative ones of Cap's existence. Back in the day, we used to joke about how the only characters who stayed dead in the Marvel Universe were Uncle Ben, Bucky, and Gwen Stacy. It was a fun joke, one that we were able to use until 2005, when Captain America (Vol. 5) began. This was the beginning of Ed Brubaker's classic run on the character and he decided to break all the rules.

Issue #6 was the one that revealed the truth about Bucky – he hadn't died when the drone bomb exploded. He was gravely injured, but found by the Soviets. They experimented on him, giving him a metal arm to replace the one he lost, the Infinity Formula to keep him hale and hearty, and brainwashed him into becoming the Winter Soldier. The return of Bucky is one of those moments that you really had to have been there for. It set the industry on fire and, because of the MCU, has become a huge moment in pop cultural history (even if we didn't know it at the time).

So, while most of the other issues on this list don't give their reveal away on the cover (there's one more that kind of does it, but you don't really understand the cover until you read the issue, so it was okay). However, the reveal in Fantastic Four #286 was too big to hide – Marvel wanted everyone to know that Jean Grey was back. Readers hadn't seen her since the end of "The Dark Phoenix Saga", when she had seemingly sacrificed her life in order to stop the Dark Phoenix from one day going crazy and destroying everything.

The original plans for "The Dark Phoenix Saga" was for Jean to survive, but editor in chief Jim Shooter had put the kibosh on that. However, plans to create a third X-Men team, this one consisting of the original members, were being made and Jean was an original member, so it was time for her to come back, with the saga's artist John Byrne writing and drawing this one. This issue was the one that established that Jean and the Phoenix were separate, leading to years of increasingly confusing retcons (maybe I shouldn't be admitting this, but I still don't understand how Jean and the Phoenix fit together) and also a few more deaths for heroine.

Avengers (Vol. 10) #1 is the newest comic on this list. It's also one of the best Marvel comics released this year. This new book spins out of Avengers: Armageddon and "Hell's Angel" from Captain America (Vol. 14). In Avengers: Armageddon, the Avengers mess up a fight against Red Hulk and the Russians – partly because of the new Miracleman – causing thousands to die in Europe. Meanwhile, in "Hell's Angels", Captain America and Doctor Doom, both of whom were in Mephisto's realm after "Doom's Shadow" and One World Under Doom , led a rebellion against the demon lord, defeating and deposing him. However, Doom took over for him and invalidated all of his contracts, a move that will have major repercussions.

Avengers (Vol. 10) #1 is the aftermath, as Mephisto, now free of his realm, starts to take back what's his from the people that he had deals with. At this point, we know that Spider-Man's deal with him for Aunt May's life has been rendered null, but we don't really know what that means for him, May, Mary Jane, or the rest of the Marvel Universe. This issue is a gamechanger right now and if you haven't read it and you love Marvel, you owe it to yourself to do so.

The X-Men's Krakoa Era was amazing , changing the team and their status quo from 2019 to 2024. It all kicked off with the two books that are one – House of X and Powers of X . These two six-issue miniseries from Jonathan Hickman, Pepe Larraz, and R.B. Silva, House of X told the story of the X-Men establishing the mutant nation of Krakoa, while Powers of X dealt with the ramifications of Krakoa across space and time. House of X #1 ended with the mutants telling humanity they had new gods and the the second issue blew the whole thing wide open.

This issue was titled "The Many Lives of Moira X" and it revealed the truth about longtime X-Men ally Moira MacTaggert. Moira wasn't a human evolutionary biologist, she was a secret mutant with the most gamechanging power of them all – every time she died, she came back to life at the moment of her birth with all her memories. The issue gave us her nine previous lives, showing how often mutants had lost the war against humanity. It changed everything we thought we knew about the X-Men.

"Fatal Attractions" was 1993's big X-Men event. The story brought back Magneto, thought dead since X-Men (Vol. 2) #3. The mutant master of magnetism had transformed Cable's satellite Graymalkin into Avalon and began to offer chosen mutants a place next to him. X-Men (Vol. 2) #25 revealed why when he released a world-crippling EMP. Thanks to their Shi'Ar technology, the X-Men were the only one able to answer leading to a battle on Avalon. We all know what happens next – Wolverine tried to kill Magneto (he did almost succeed), but got his adamantium skeleton ripped out because he decided to sass Mags instead of stab him in the throat, which then led to Xavier mindwiping Magneto.

All of this led to Wolverine (Vol. 2) #75, which saw the X-Men try to keep Magneto alive as they basically crash-landed at the mansion. Logan survives – even saving Jean Grey when she's almost pulled out of the X-Jet – and is put under the care of Moira and Beast. However, he has none of that and goes to the Danger Room to test himself out against some combat robots. Then he pops his claws. Gone were the razor sharp adamantium talons and in their place are bone claws. This was the beginning of Wolverine's bone claw era, six years of stories about Wolvie learning to do more with less, including some of the best Wolverine stories ever . Remember, he was Marvel's most popular character of the day and they dropped this kind of change on him for six years. Marvel used to be something.

What do you think is the biggest game-changing reveal in Marvel history? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: The Traitors: New Blood Frustrated Me, So I Have Some Suggestions For Season 2
articles.summary: Do better with the editing, please.
articles.content:
The Traitors: New Blood returns for a second season in 2027. I am excited because I gladly welcome any Traitors . However, New Blood may be my least favorite of the franchise.

For a long time, people used cliffhangers to entice readers or viewers to continuously return. It’s been part of the reality TV landscape for many decades. However, it’s not the only way to ensure viewership. The original The Traitors uses cliffhangers quite often, but it never felt as tedious as it does on The Traitors: New Blood .

A major appeal of The Traitors US is that it’s full of familiar faces . We know these reality TV stars, so we can get excited to see what they bring to the show. The Traitors: New Blood has some familiar influencers, but they are not as recognizable as reality TV stars and celebrities. Therefore, we want to get to know them.

Fruitgate starts very interestingly and produced one of the season’s best episodes. However, the constant talk about it made me grow sour about the topic. It made me question if it’s fair that the Traitors have to make so many risky moves.

articles.summary: It looks like it might be another L in the books for Zack Snyder. And while it's true that the movie he's potentially lost out on has been stuck in development hell for years, and that he was only attached back in June of this year, it can't feel great to no longer be associated […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It looks like it might be another L in the books for Zack Snyder . And while it's true that the movie he's potentially lost out on has been stuck in development hell for years, and that he was only attached back in June of this year, it can't feel great to no longer be associated with the project—however that came about. The details are a little hazy, but it was initially reported by World of Reel that John Carpenter has said that Snyder is no longer on board for the Escape from New York remake and that he's been replaced by none other than Robert Rodriguez.

Snyder's involvement had been the only forward movement the project had seen in years, though it had previously had all sorts of names attached to it, including Radio Silence, Leigh Whannell, Brett Ratner, Len Wiseman, Breck Eisner, and Neil Cross. And when he sat down for an interview with Dropping Names , Carpenter, the original Escape from New York 's creator, revealed that Snyder was no longer involved, saying cryptically, "He’s not anymore, but he’s trying to get back. He’s trying to get back. We’ll see. Nice man. I liked him.” What exactly the filmmaker means by "he's trying to get back" is anyone's guess ( though surely some are hoping it's Snyderverse-related ).

It's still way too up in the air to know anything for sure, but some fans are definitely questioning why the production would swap out one director who finds himself on a losing streak for another on a seemingly worse streak. "I already saw a movie directed by Zack Snyder where people have to go into a cordoned-off zone for action hijinks. Somehow, even with a zombie tiger, it was f*cking tedious," said one fan about Snyder. As for Rodriguez, others were quick to add that he hasn't had a good film since Sin City , which he directed alongside Frank Miller.

Though some are skeptical about Snyder no longer being involved in the project, especially as this episode was shot months before its release. One listener said, "That’s not at all what was said on Dropping Names, and the episode was shot months ago. They specifically refer to Sam Neil being alive. In terms of the 'trying to get back' quote. That was about Snyder’s career, not this film. So, I’m sorry, we’re still stuck for now." And "stuck" is a great descriptor for how fans of the original (those who even want a remake) feel about Snyder as the prospective director. Overall, it's unclear what any of this really means, though it's worth noting that if Snyder isn't actually off the project, there's still Rodriguez waiting in the wings with an entirely different idea and script that Carpenter has reportedly signed off on.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Fans Disappointed After Nintendo Removes Entire Feature
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake fans are dissapointed over a feature in the N64 original that was not carried forward to the new Nintendo Switch 2 remake. Other than some cut content here and there, the new Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is a very faithful remake of the original […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake fans are dissapointed over a feature in the N64 original that was not carried forward to the new Nintendo Switch 2 remake. Other than some cut content here and there, the new Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is a very faithful remake of the original game on N64. And you would expect it to be. When the game was re-released on GameCube, and then later remade on the 3DS, this was also the case, and it's the case because the N64 game is one of the best games ever made, in conversations with the likes of Red Dead Redemption 2 , various Grand Theft Auto games including the new GTA 6 , Half-Life 2 , BioShock , SoulCalibur, both Super Mario Galaxy games, fellow Zelda game Breath of the Wild , and a few others.

The new Nintendo Switch 2 remake is not a one-for-one remake, though. Not at all. Most of what has been changed has either gone largely unnoticed, or they are changes fans actually appreciate. This isn't the case with one change, though.

One of the top posts on the Ocarina of Time Reddit page this week is a post lamenting that the custom name save files of the original were not carried forward with the Nintendo Switch 2 remake. For those who didn't play the original game on the N64, when you started a new game, you were presented with a name-entry screen. You could put anything into this. And whatever you put became the name of Link. As a result, that name was substituted into dialogue. Obviously, players had fun with this.

The post above shot to the top of its respective Reddit page, so it is clearly a sentiment other fans of the Nintendo series share. If there was any doubt about this, the comments reinforce this.

"This is probably the only thing so far I don't like from the remake. It's probably due to the voices saying 'Link'."

Another comment adds, "A friend of mine once suggested I name him My Dude. I was confused at first, but trusted my friend and did as he asked. Link has had no other name since then."

What is lost on players who have come to The Legend of Zelda series in the modern era is that there was a time in the series where Link didn't have much distinction and personality, and was rather an avatar for the player. The character was iconic, but there was not much to him.

That said, the reason this was no doubt removed was because players could easily take advantage of it. Now, Nintendo could put restrictions in place, but then there would be blowback about that, and players would probably find a way around these restrictions. Further, some of the aforementioned removed content are the Super Mario easter eggs, which Nintendo removed because they want the game to be more immersive and mature. This same line of thinking would no doubt apply here as well. Maybe this feature will return in the leaked DLC , but it's highly unlikely.

articles.title: I’m In My Feelings Over The Chat Alfonso Ribeiro Had With Harry Shum Jr. And Jenna Johnson After Their DWTS Elimination
articles.summary: I'm emotional all over again.
articles.content:
The final weeks of Dancing with the Stars always feature really tough eliminations. However, the last few on the 2026 TV schedule have been brutal. Specifically, Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson went home during the semifinals after getting perfect scores for their Paso Doble and Glee- themed Quickstep . Now, co-host Alfonso Ribeiro has opened up about the conversation he had with the pair following their shocking elimination, and I'm feeling emotional all over again.

I’m also saddened for them. While Harry and Jenna always had some of the best routines of every episode, their DWTS journey was plagued by some controversy and intense online discourse. Of course, there was liftgate , which led to a comment from Johnson’s husband and fellow pro Val Chmerkovskiy that got him suspended from the show for a week. There was also the ongoing debate regarding the amount of dance experience Harry Shum Jr. had before doing DWTS .

It does feel like the mirrorball trophy could be anyone's. They’re all pretty good, and it’s clear that everyone left has a very devoted fan base. So, it’s unclear who will win, and an argument can be made for any of them. I mean, when I think about all this, there’s part of me that wants Amber Glenn to win , and thinks she can do it based on her scores and consistency. Meanwhile, Connor Wood’s social media likes prove he has a very devoted group of fans behind him that could help make up for his lower scores and push him across the finish line. Seriously, it’s anyone’s game.

I totally see his point. DWTS is a massive time commitment, and it’s an intense experience both physically and mentally. These stars put their everything into it, and so it’s sad to see any of them not reach the end.

articles.title: I Thought People Would Recognize Andrew Scott From Sherlock, But Another Role Comes Up Way More
articles.summary: His appeal goes far beyond Baker Street.
articles.content:
There's no denying Andrew Scott delivered one of the most compelling portrayals of Moriarty opposite Benedict Cumberbatch in what remains one of the standout adaptations of Sherlock Holmes . The show ran on the BBC for 4 seasons, and fans are still holding out hope for a 5th run . I honestly thought this would be the role he was most recognized for, but it turns out that's not the case. Without hesitation, Scott told me it's actually the “Hot Priest” from Fleabag .

I'm glad to see I'm not alone in this. For me, and clearly for a lot more people than I thought, Scott is the ‘Hot Priest.' He takes a man of the cloth and makes him layered, complicated, charismatic, and, above all, very sexy. If you've seen Fleabag , I'm sure the line “Kneel. Just kneel.” is burned into your brain for all eternity, just like it is mine. He clearly has a knack for making even a single line stick with audiences, as is the case with his one line in Saving Private Ryan .

Piper is spot on. I watched it, and there is no other word to describe that scene. But Scott is so much more than "hot." He is, in my opinion, a once-in-a-generation talent, and the roles he plays are memorable. He has this rare ability to make even the biggest performances feel incredibly personal, almost like he's speaking directly to each individual person watching. That's especially true in Elsinore . I think he's going to give Robert Pattinson a run for his money this Oscar season . Honest.

articles.title: Skydance Already Has the Perfect Script to Relaunch the Justice League, And It Almost Happened 20 Years Ago
articles.summary: Skydance wants to get the Justice League back in theaters, and the studio may already have the right script sitting in a drawer somewhere. With James Gunn and Peter Safran departing as DC Studios executives, incoming studio chief Jeremy Latcham has reportedly been tasked with getting DC’s biggest superheroes together as soon as he can. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Skydance wants to get the Justice League back in theaters, and the studio may already have the right script sitting in a drawer somewhere. With James Gunn and Peter Safran departing as DC Studios executives, incoming studio chief Jeremy Latcham has reportedly been tasked with getting DC’s biggest superheroes together as soon as he can. Rather than start from scratch, Skydance could dust off a movie that almost got made 20 years ago.

Before Zack Snyder brought DC's biggest heroes together in 2017, Mad Max: Fury Road director George Miller almost made Justice League: Mortal . Warner Bros. pulled the plug when the movie was fully cast and deep into preproduction. Its completed screenplay eventually leaked online , revealing an ambitious superhero movie that might work even better today.

In 2007, Warner Bros. hired Miller to direct Justice League: Mortal from a screenplay by Kieran and Michele Mulroney. Unlike the Marvel Cinematic Universe, which spent years introducing its heroes before bringing the Avengers together, Miller’s film would have dropped viewers into a world where DC’s superheroes were already up and running. No backstory required.

The cast featured D.J. Cotrona as Superman and Adam Brody as the Flash, who would later reunite as members of the Shazam family, playing the adult superhero versions of Pedro Peña and Freddy Freeman, respectively. Common was cast as Green Lantern John Stewart. His imposing performance as Robert Sims in Silo offers a taste of what we missed. Miller later cast his Wonder Woman, Megan Gale, as the Valkyrie in Mad Max: Fury Road . Santiago Cabrera, originally cast as Aquaman , went on to star in Star Trek: Picard , while Hugh Keays-Byrne, cast as Martian Manhunter, played Immortan Joe in Fury Road . Jay Baruchel was set to play Maxwell Lord, with Teresa Palmer as Talia al Ghul. Palmer may be the only casting choice that truly needs to be corrected. A French Talia? Of course. But an Australian Talia al Ghul? I don't know, mate.

The 2007 writers' strike, as well as issues with Australian production incentives, derailed the film. Miller went on to create Fury Road , but Justice League: Mortal left a screenplay worth revisiting. Armie Hammer, who was prepared to take on the role of Batman. Below you can see some of the concept art and storyboards from the film, plus Kevin Smith talking to Hammer about almost starring in Miller’s movie.

Adapting the Tower of Babel Arc From JLA Ra's al Ghul uses Batman's contingency plans against the League in Mark Waid and Howard Porter's JLA: Tower of Babel . Mortal combines that premise with the events leading up to Infinite Crisis . Maxwell Lord hijacks Batman's Brother Eye surveillance system and uses his telepathic abilities to turn Superman against his teammates. The screenplay also puts a twist on one of the most controversial moments from that era of DC Comics, when Wonder Woman snaps Lord's neck to free Superman from his control. That moment occurred in Wonder Woman #219, the conclusion of the four-part Superman: Sacrifice crossover. In Mortal , however, it's Batman who snaps Lord's neck.

Zack Snyder would later echo the comic book moment in Man of Steel , with Superman snapping General Zod's neck to save innocent lives. James Gunn famously detested this villainous version of Lord . Given the uncertainty surrounding Sean Gunn's future in the role, Skydance could revisit the darker interpretation introduced in Countdown to Infinite Crisis .

From David S. Goyer and Justin Marks' Green Arrow: Escape from Super Max to George Miller's Justice League: Mortal , Skydance has an abundance of abandoned DC projects it could revisit before commissioning new ones. Super Max would have seen Oliver Queen stripped of his identity and imprisoned alongside some of the DC Universe's most notorious supervillains.

Guillermo del Toro completed a screenplay for Justice League Dark that would have seen John Constantine assemble a team including Swamp Thing, Zatanna, and Deadman. Del Toro even envisioned frequent collaborator Doug Jones as Deadman . Following the success of Frankenstein , why not give the director another crack at DC's supernatural characters?

Ava DuVernay and comic book writer Tom King were also developing a film around Jack Kirby's New Gods. King has since returned to Kirby's Fourth World as the showrunner of Mister Miracle , an animated series starring Josh Hutcherson and Mackenzie Davis as Scott Free and Big Barda. The series is still in production, and it's entirely possible that some of the ideas King explored with DuVernay have found their way into the animated series. Skydance could build on that work with a live-action New Gods movie.

Skydance has not yet said what its future plans are for the DC Universe. But if Man of Tomorrow leaves the studio with a Justice League worth keeping, then Justice League: Mortal provides the perfect opportunity to tear it apart. What abandoned DC project would you like to see resuscitated by Skydance? Let us know in the comments below.

articles.title: Yu Yu Hakusho Needs a Modern Anime Revival for One Main Reason
articles.summary: Shueisha / Pierrot In recent years, there's been a massive uptick in classic anime series receiving new-and-improved reboots that aim to deliver modern animation, stories that stay more closely aligned to the story's original source material, and even new vocal performances from legacy cast members. These successful reboots, which include the likes of Ranma 1/2 and Urusei Yatsura, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google In recent years, there's been a massive uptick in classic anime series receiving new-and-improved reboots that aim to deliver modern animation , stories that stay more closely aligned to the story's original source material, and even new vocal performances from legacy cast members. These successful reboots, which include the likes of Ranma 1/2 and Urusei Yatsura , are introducing an old-school style of anime to new-age fans looking to sink their teeth into a wider variety of storytelling. One of the more popular classics that's yet to receive a proper re-adaptation is Yu Yu Hakusho , originally created by Hunter x Hunter 's mangaka Yoshihiro Togashi. Yu Yu Hakusho 's original anime adaptation from Studio Pierrot ran for 112 episodes beginning in 1992, and despite how iconic the series is, desperately deserves a fresh adaptation.

Yu Yu Hakusho follows Yusuke Urameshi, a 14-year-old delinquent who dies saving a young boy from a car accident. After being sent to the afterlife and proving his worth, Yusuke is given the chance to return back to the world of the living to work as a Spirit Detective who investigates paranormal threats and demons threatening to harm normal humans. Contrasting from other anime released during the same era, Yu Yu Hakusho stayed surprisingly close to the source material, however, the series did cut some of the manga's earlier chapters short and expanded upon other story arcs with some additional content not present in Togashi's original work. While there's nothing inherently wrong with the original adaptation of Yu Yu Haksuho , the series could benefit greatly from getting a high quality reboot.

With the anime community's rapid growth spurt over the last decade, new anime fans are clamoring season-to-season to find new shows to latch onto. While there have been plenty of great new ideas hitting these lineups, seeing beloved classics return with modernized animation techniques and production teams have given a number of old-school series a fresh audience to bring them back to life . Yu Yu Hakusho is the perfect show for audiences right now; the series' focuses on themes of personal growth intertwined with the emotional and psychological cost of violence within a supernatural conflict between humans and demons.

These kinds of stories have been deeply resonating with anime fans — with similar shows like Jujutsu Kaisen becoming some of the biggest pop culture phenomenons on the planet. One of the bigger questions surrounding a re-adaptation of Yu Yu Haksuho would be what studio and directors would be capable of pulling off such a large scale project . If fans were to receive a complete remake that adapted all 19-volumes of Togashi's original work, the show would need a production studio capable of taking on longterm productions without fear of quality dips or production stalls.

While MAPPA is a fan-favorite dream studio for imagining projects like this, other popular studios like Studio Bones, which has handled long-form shonen series like My Hero Academia and Mob Psycho 100 , or even Wit Studio, who made a name for themselves with their adaptations of Vinland Saga , Spy x Family , and Attack on Titan stand out as possible choices. That said, Yu Yu Hakusho may find a better home with Madhouse — known for their stunning adaptation of Frieren: Beyond Journey's End , and perhaps in this particular case, for their work on 2011's adaptation of Hunter x Hunter .

Yu Yu Hakusho wouldn't be the first of Togashi's manga to receive a reboot that makes a cultural statement for anime fans. The 2011 reboot of Togashi's Hunter x Hunter stole anime fans from that decade and beyond's hearts , and for good reason. The Madhouse-produced series had a 148-episode run that spanned three years, and beautifully translated Togashi's signature illustrations to animation. Not to mention, Hunter x Hunter 's 2011 reboot only helped in skyrocketing the popularity of the original work more, which now has well over 100-million copies in circulation, making it one of only around twenty-five other series to reach the same level of acclaim.

While Yu Yu Hakusho is an incredible series by its own merit, having 19-collected volumes after running in Weekly Shonen Jump magazine for four years . Even years after the series came to an end, the manga reportedly has 78-million copies in circulation. Yu Yu Hakusho has consistently ranked in popularity polls around the globe like Nielsen BookScan in North America, with multiple volumes from the series ranking week-to-week. In Japan alone, Yu Yu Hakusho earned the Shogakukan Manga Award in 1993's shonen category and ranked 17th in 2021's TV Asahi's Manga Sosenkyo poll wherein 150,000 manga readers voted on their top 100 series.

Needless to say, a high quality, action-packed reboot of Yu Yu Hakusho would immediately grab the attention of thousands of anime fans around the globe and dominate the anime community. Would you want to see a new version of Yu Yu Hakusho ? Let us know your thoughts about it in the comments.

Whether the starlet is out and about or not, though, her music consistently plays across the airwaves. So what's it like for Grande to hear her work in public? Well, the Wicked actress got real about the wildest place she heard her music, and believe me when I say I was not expecting her to mention a bikini wax while explaining.

With the former Nickelodeon actress being one of the best-selling artists of all time and having ten Billboard Top 100 singles, she gets a lot of airtime. So it's pretty much a given that Grande would hear her own music now and then. As a matter of fact, when Harper’s Bazaar asked Grande about the wildest place she ever heard her own songs, she mentioned a wax:

Yeah, I was one time getting a bikini wax. And the song came on, and I didn’t think [the bikini wax employee] knew who I was at all. I never assume that anyone does.

Grande continued to mimic the satisfied look of the wax specialist, who also said to her, “And my kids love your show!” While the former child has spoken before about how fame tends to complicate her music career , it looks like it can also come with some surreal and somewhat funny encounters with fans as well.

A celebrity like Hugh Jackman can relate to the joy of hearing his own music in public. Months after his movie, The Greatest Showman, premiered, he recalled overhearing the film’s soundtrack as he was making his way to the door of an apartment or hotel. I can imagine it feeling like such an honor for an artist when someone is enjoying their work in some form or another.

Let's also be real, as Ariana Grande ’s music is easy to love, given her immense talent. Per a fun fact about Grande , five-time Grammy winner Gloria Estefan spotted her talent when she was 8 years old and singing on a cruise ship. I think it's fair to say Estefan knows talent when she sees it.

Back in 2019, her single “Thank U, Next” broke an impressive record , as it surpassed Ed Sheeran and Cardi B.’s streaming sales. And, this year, the “Positions” singer’s Eternal Sunshine Tour was her second highest-grossing tour she’s had, earning $107.9 million.

Now, on the heels of that top-selling tour ended in, Grande can celebrate her role in the highly anticipated Focker-In-Law . The film sees Grande play the fiancée of Greg Focker’s son, who also ends up having a rivalry with her future father-in-law. It’ll be exciting to see “The Way” singer go back to her comedy roots and mix it up with stars like Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro .

I wonder whether Grande's music was played on set and if so, which tracks were selected. Personally, I think a set seems like a more obvious place for her to hear her songs as opposed to a place where she can get a bikini wax. That aside, check out the Oscar nominee in Focker-in-Law when it opens on November 25th amid the 2026 movie release .
